title_en: Jiangxi Zhenye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Jiangxi Guoli Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. — dispute over a construction project contract
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 34 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Litigation, a party shall submit evidentiary materials to the people's court within the time limit for evidence submission. If the party fails to submit within the time limit, it is deemed to have waived the right to present evidence, and the people's court may find the facts of the case based on the evidence provided by the other party. full_text_en:
Jiangxi Zhenye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v.

Jiangxi Guoli Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project contract

【Ruling Summary】

According to the provisions of Article 34 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, a party shall submit evidentiary materials to the people's court within the time limit for adducing evidence. If a party fails to submit evidence within the time limit, it is deemed to have waived the right to adduce evidence, and the people's court may determine the facts of the case based on the evidence provided by the opposing party. However, the party deemed to have waived the right to adduce evidence still retains the right of defense in accordance with the law, and the people's court shall review the defense in accordance with the law; if the defense is well-founded, it shall be adopted and supported.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 52

Appellant (original defendant): Jiangxi Zhenye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 98, Erqi North Road, Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Liang Yaoke, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Tang Zhongzan, lawyer of Jiangxi Golden Phoenix Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wan Yijiao, lawyer of Jiangxi Golden Phoenix Law Firm.

Appellee (original plaintiff): Jiangxi Guoli Construction Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 10, Tuanjie Road, Chaoyangzhou, Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Guozai, Chairman of the company.

Agent ad litem: Xiong Shaoyun, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Kaiding, lawyer of Beijing Zhonglun Jintong Law Firm.

The appellant, Jiangxi Zhenye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenye Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2005) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 5 rendered by the Jiangxi High People's Court in the dispute over a construction project contract with the appellee, Jiangxi Guoli Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guoli Company), appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a panel and held a public hearing on September 12, 2006. Tang Zhongzan and Wan Yijiao, agents ad litem of Zhenye Company, and Wang Kaiding and Min Hanqi, agents ad litem of Guoli Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found upon trial: On June 6, 2002, the People's Government of Jinxian County, Jiangxi Province (hereinafter referred to as Jinxian County People's Government) and Shenzhen Zhenchang Investment Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenchang Company) entered into the "Contract for the Development of Jinxian County Government Compound and New District Construction". On June 8, 2002, Zhenchang Company issued a power of attorney to the Jinxian County People's Government, entrusting Zhenye Company with full authority to be responsible for the development, operation, and construction of the project. On June 12, 2002, Zhenye Company applied for the establishment of the "General Headquarters for the Development of the Jinxian County Government Compound and Administrative Center Construction Project", which was duly approved by the Jinxian County Administration for Industry and Commerce. The General Headquarters for the Development of the Jinxian County Government Compound and Administrative Center Construction Project entered into three "Construction Project Construction Contracts" and their "Supplementary Agreements" with Guoli Company on September 1, 2002, February 25, 2003, and March 10, 2003, respectively. The construction projects were the Jinxian County Administrative Center Construction Project: Government Building, Archives, Cafeteria, and Hotel. The contracted scope of work included civil engineering (foundation, structure, roofing, masonry, plastic-steel windows, plastering, floor finishing, water and electrical installation, etc.). The total contract price for the three contracts was RMB 14.24 million. The project adopted an adjustable price. The method and scope of price adjustment were: adjustments based on construction drawings, change notices, and site instruction sheets; the adjustment range shall not exceed the final settlement price between Zhenye Company and the Jinxian County People's Government; the final price shall be based on the cost approved by the Jinxian County People's Government. The contract stipulated that after the full completion and settlement of the construction projects undertaken by Guoli Company, Zhenye Company shall pay 90% of the project cost within half a year, pay 7% upon the expiration of the civil works warranty period, and the remaining 3% shall be retained as project quality warranty deposit. Guoli Company agreed to make an 8% concession on the total project cost. The settlement basis was the 2001 "National Unified Building (Installation) Engineering Quota" (Jiangxi Province Unit Price Estimation Table), with fees calculated at Category III. Quality standards: the Government Building and Archives were required to be municipal-level quality projects; if they failed to achieve municipal-level quality, a penalty of 3% of the total project cost would be deducted. The Cafeteria and Hotel were required to be up-to-standard projects. The contract provisions on project completion settlement stipulated: The employer (Zhenye Company) shall verify the completion settlement report and settlement materials submitted by the contractor (Guoli Company) within 28 days, giving confirmation or proposing modifications. If the employer fails to pay the project completion settlement amount without justifiable reasons within 28 days after receiving the completion settlement report and settlement materials, interest on the overdue project payment shall be calculated from the 29th day at the contractor's contemporaneous bank lending rate, and the employer shall bear liability for breach of contract. During construction, Zhenye Company subcontracted the roofing and water and electrical installation works, which were within the contract scope, to other companies. Zhenye Company received the project settlement reports for the Jinxian County Administrative Center Construction Project — Archives, Government Building, Cafeteria, and Hotel Building, submitted by Guoli Company on September 23, 2004, November 8, 2004, and December 30, 2004, respectively. The settlement reports showed a total project cost of RMB 24,742,895.8. On August 25, 2004, the Government Building, Archives, Cafeteria, and Hotel constructed by Guoli Company passed completion acceptance and were put into use. The Cafeteria and Hotel Building were inspected and rated as up-to-standard projects; the Government Building and Archives Building were rated as municipal-level quality structural projects by the Nanchang Construction Project Quality Supervision Station; the Government Building was rated as a municipal-level quality project by the Nanchang Urban and Rural Construction Commission. On April 1, 2005, the General Headquarters for the Development of the Jinxian County Government Compound and Administrative Center Construction Project issued a notice to all construction units, requiring them to promptly provide complete and valid settlement data to enter the settlement process. By the date of filing this lawsuit, Zhenye Company had paid a total of RMB 12.64 million in project payments to Guoli Company. The project settlement unilaterally prepared by Guoli Company showed that Zhenye Company still owed Guoli Company project payments of RMB 12,102,895.8.

The court of first instance also found: Article 11 of the "Contract for the Development of Jinxian County Government Compound and New District Construction" entered into between Zhenchang Company and the Jinxian County People's Government stipulated: "After the new district construction project passes completion acceptance, the parties shall conduct financial settlement, which must be completed within one month from the date of acceptance." The project settlement between Zhenchang Company and the Jinxian County People's Government has not yet been carried out.

The court of first instance notified the parties that the time limit for adducing evidence was before August 15, 2005, and conducted two exchanges of evidence between the parties on September 12 and September 29, 2005. During this period, Zhenye Company did not file a motion for judicial appraisal of the project cost involved in this case. On October 8, 2005, Zhenye Company submitted a written application to the court of first instance, requesting a judicial appraisal of the project cost in this case. During the transfer for appraisal, Zhenye Company raised objections to the scope of the appraisal and failed to pay the appraisal fees within the time limit required by the notice. The Judicial Technical Office of the court of first instance returned the case on March 17, 2006.

On December 13, 2005, Guoli Company filed a motion for advance execution with the court of first instance. After review, the court of first instance issued a civil ruling (2005) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 5-2 on January 16, 2006, ordering Zhenye Company to pay RMB 2 million to Guoli Company. This amount has been executed.

Because the project payments in dispute were not settled, Guoli Company filed a lawsuit with the Xihu District People's Court of Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province (hereinafter referred to as Xihu District People's Court) on April 27, 2005. After the Xihu District People's Court accepted the case, Zhenye Company raised an objection to jurisdiction. On May 23, 2005, the Xihu District People's Court transferred the case to the Jiangxi High People's Court. Guoli Company's claims were: to order Zhenye Company to pay the outstanding project cost of RMB 12.10 million and interest of RMB 900,000; and to order Zhenye Company to bear the case acceptance fee and property preservation fee in this case.

The court of first instance held that: The General Headquarters for the Development of the Jinxian County Government Compound and Administrative Center Construction Project, established by Zhenye Company upon application and approved by the administrative department for industry and commerce, entered into the three "Construction Project Construction Contracts" and their "Supplementary Agreements" with Guoli Company. These represented the true intentions of the parties, and their contents did not violate prohibitive provisions of national laws or administrative regulations; therefore, they should be valid and binding. Since the General Headquarters lacked legal personality, its civil liability should be borne by Zhenye Company. Zhenye Company did not object to its status as a party in this case, and the court confirmed this. Guoli Company performed its obligations in accordance with the contracts, completing the civil engineering works for the Government Building, Archives, Cafeteria, and Hotel within the contracted scope. After the project was completed, Zhenye Company paid part of the project cost to Guoli Company. During the settlement process, Guoli Company submitted the project settlement reports for the Government Building, Archives, Cafeteria, and Hotel to Zhenye Company. The completion settlement clauses in the construction project contracts stipulated that the employer shall verify the completion settlement report and materials submitted by the contractor within 28 days, giving confirmation or proposing modifications. If the employer fails to pay the project completion settlement amount without justifiable reasons within 28 days after receiving the completion settlement report and materials, interest on the overdue project payments shall be calculated from the 29th day at the contractor's contemporaneous bank lending rate, and the employer shall bear liability for breach of contract. Article 20 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Contracts provides: "If the parties agree that upon the employer's failure to respond within the agreed time limit after receiving the completion settlement documents, the settlement documents shall be deemed to have been accepted, the matter shall be dealt with according to the agreement. If the contractor requests settlement of the project cost in accordance with the completion settlement documents, it shall be supported." Guoli Company's claim for Zhenye Company to pay the outstanding project cost was consistent with the agreement between the parties and the above-mentioned judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court, and should be supported in accordance with the law. After receiving the project settlement reports submitted by Guoli Company, Zhenye Company did not raise any objections within the time limit stipulated in the contract. Zhenye Company's defense that Guoli Company did not submit complete settlement data, causing the settlement work to proceed normally, with the fault entirely on Guoli Company, was untenable. Although the construction project contract signed by the parties provided for an adjustable price, with the method and scope of price adjustment being adjustments based on construction drawings, change notices, and site instruction sheets, with the adjustment range not exceeding the settlement price between Zhenye Company and the Jinxian County People's Government, and the final price based on the cost approved by the Jinxian County People's Government, the settlement between Zhenye Company and the Jinxian County People's Government for the project cost had not yet been carried out, and the cost ultimately approved by the Jinxian County People's Government could not be determined. When judicial appraisal was conducted for the adjustable part of the project cost in this case, Zhenye Company failed to pay the appraisal fees within the time limit required by the court's entrusted appraisal department, which should be deemed as Zhenye Company waiving its motion for appraisal in the exercise of litigation rights. In its claims, Guoli Company requested an order for Zhenye Company to pay the outstanding project cost of RMB 12.10 million. During the proceedings, Guoli Company submitted a written statement explaining that at the time of filing the lawsuit, it had not deducted the 8% concession (amounting to RMB 1,979,200) from the project cost as provided in the supplementary agreement signed by the parties, and that the actual outstanding project cost owed by Zhenye Company was RMB 10,120,800. This was Guoli Company's disposition of its own civil rights within the scope provided by law, and the court of first instance approved it. After deducting the RMB 2 million already paid by Zhenye Company to Guoli Company through advance execution, the amount Zhenye Company should pay to Guoli Company was RMB 8,120,800. Guoli Company's claim for interest of RMB 900,000 on the outstanding project cost was not supported by a calculation basis, so the amount of interest on the outstanding project cost could only be determined according to general interest calculation rules. Moreover, according to the contract, the outstanding project cost claimed by Guoli Company also included the 3% project quality warranty deposit. The contract stipulated that the warranty period for civil works was one year. Although the warranty period had expired, according to the contract, no interest was calculated on the returned warranty deposit. Therefore, the court of first instance partially did not support Guoli Company's claim for interest. Accordingly, the court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 60, 107, and 109 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 17 and 20 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Contracts, Article 25 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, and Article 13 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled: Zhenye Company shall pay Guoli Company RMB 8,120,800 in project cost and interest (the interest amount shall be calculated from January 28, 2005, at the same-period same-type loan interest rate published by the People's Bank of China until full payment, but no interest shall be calculated on the 3% warranty deposit in the project cost) within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment. The case acceptance fee of RMB 75,010 and the property preservation fee of RMB 65,520, totaling RMB 140,530, shall be borne by Zhenye Company in the amount of 90%, i.e., RMB 126,477; and by Guoli Company in the amount of 10%, i.e., RMB 14,053.

Zhenye Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of the first instance, filed an appeal with this Court on May 28, 2006, requesting the revocation of the civil judgment (2005) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 5 of the Jiangxi High People's Court, dismissal of all of Guoli Company's claims in the first instance, and that Guoli Company bear all litigation costs in both instances. The main grounds for appeal were: 1. The judgment of the first instance erred in finding facts and applying the law. The engineering change orders were not confirmed by the construction party, but the judgment of the first instance confirmed all six engineering change orders provided by Guoli Company; the finding that Guoli Company submitted the settlement data for the Jinxian County Government Building project to Zhenye Company on November 8, 2004, based on a work contact letter, was also erroneous; and the failure to recognize the validity of the "Meeting Minutes" in question and their effect on Guoli Company was an error in the application of the law. 2. The settlement data submitted by Guoli Company were incomplete, and Guoli Company delayed in completing them. The conditions for Guoli Company to demand payment of the project cost had not been fulfilled, and Guoli Company had no right to demand payment from Zhenye Company. The judgment of the first instance erroneously applied the judicial interpretation on disputes over construction project contracts, using the unilateral settlement report as the basis for payment. 3. The project settlement report contained calculation errors, overstating the project cost by RMB 11,378,038.05, including one item overstated by RMB 1,879,343.98. 4. The first-instance proceedings were procedurally flawed, including the improper property preservation and advance execution against Zhenye Company, and the failure to conduct a judicial appraisal of the entire project cost. The project in question was a government-invested project, with the Jinxian County People's Government as the project owner and Zhenchang Company as the construction agent; the court should have notified them to participate in the proceedings.

In its response, Guoli Company requested that the original judgment be affirmed and that Zhenye Company's appeal be dismissed. The main grounds were: 1. On August 25, 2004, the project in question constructed by Guoli Company passed completion acceptance and was delivered for use. Zhenye Company signed for and received the project completion settlement reports submitted by Guoli Company, which fully indicated that Zhenye Company confirmed the contents of Guoli Company's work contact letters. Within the time limit stipulated in the contract, Zhenye Company did not raise any objections to the settlement reports. 2. The time limit for adducing evidence set by the court of first instance was August 15, 2005. Zhenye Company did not file a motion for appraisal until October 8 of the same year, violating the relevant provisions on evidence. After the court of first instance agreed to the appraisal, Zhenye Company refused to pay the appraisal fees, causing the appraisal to fail, and should bear the consequences of failure to adduce evidence. 3. Regarding the engineering change orders: The six engineering change orders were stamped by both Guoli Company and Zhenye Company, indicating mutual agreement on the change in project quantities; Zhenye Company should pay for the changes accordingly. The relationship between Guoli Company and Zhenye Company was that of a construction project contract, while the relationship between Zhenye Company and the Jinxian County People's Government was that of a real estate development contract. Guoli Company did not enter into any agreement with the Jinxian County People's Government. According to the relativity of the rights and obligations of each party, the obligation to submit engineering change orders to the Jinxian County People's Government rested with Zhenye Company, as the obligor. The project in question had passed completion acceptance and was delivered for use. The Jinxian County People's Government was one of the acceptance units, which was sufficient to confirm the entire project quantity. 4. The contract between Guoli Company and Zhenye Company clearly stipulated a settlement period. Zhenye Company did not confirm or modify the settlement data submitted by Guoli Company within the agreed settlement period, and Zhenye Company should bear liability for breach of contract. 5. Regarding the validity of the "Meeting Minutes" dated January 8, 2005: Although Xiong Xiaoping was the project manager appointed by Guoli Company, according to the contract (General Terms, Article 1.5), the project manager was only responsible for construction management and performing the contract, and had no authority to conclude, modify, or terminate contracts on behalf of Guoli Company. The "Meeting Minutes" had no legal binding force on Guoli Company. 6. The court of first instance's rulings on property preservation and advance execution, the termination of the judicial appraisal, and the deduction of the 8% concession project cost in the judgment were all in accordance with the law.

The court of second instance found upon investigation: In this case, the "Archives Building" referred to the Archives as stipulated in the "Construction Project Construction Contract"; Zhenye Company was not a party to the "Meeting Minutes" dated January 8, 2005; due to calculation errors in the project settlement report prepared by Guoli Company, the project cost was overstated by RMB 1,879,343.98.

On December 26, 2006, Guoli Company changed its litigation representative: entrusting its employee Xiong Shaoyun as its litigation agent in the second instance of this case, and terminating the agency contract with Min Hanqi.

During the second-instance proceedings, on February 2, 2007, Guoli Company issued a "Confirmation Letter", clearly stating that it waived the interest of RMB 600,000 on the project cost; waived the overstated project cost of RMB 1,879,343.98 due to calculation errors in the project settlement report, totaling RMB 2,479,343.98.

Other facts found by this Court in the second instance are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

We hold that: The three "Construction Project Construction Contracts" and their "Supplementary Agreements" entered into between Zhenye Company and Guoli Company represent the true intentions of the parties, and their contents do not violate laws or regulations; they should be deemed valid and binding. The above contracts are binding on both parties. The main issues in dispute between the parties during the second instance were:

(1) Whether the conditions for payment of the project cost have been fulfilled. Guoli Company has performed its contractual obligations, and the project in question has passed acceptance and been delivered for use. Zhenye Company does not dispute the quality of the project. Subsequently, Guoli Company submitted the completion settlement documents to Zhenye Company in accordance with the contract. Within 28 days after receiving the completion settlement data, Zhenye Company neither expressed approval nor proposed modifications, violating the provisions of Article 33(3) of the standard "Construction Project Construction Contract" text formulated by the Ministry of Construction, which was chosen by the parties. From the 29th day, the conditions for payment of the project cost were fulfilled. Zhenye Company's breach of contract could not prevent the fulfillment of the conditions for payment of the project cost.

(2) Calculation of the Project Payment. Since the contract in this case provides that the project price is adjustable, the parties have a dispute over the adjustment. Zhenye Company argues that the first-instance judgment erroneously confirmed all six change orders submitted by Guoli Company, pointing out that two of them lacked the signature of the construction unit's representative, and one lacked the signature of the design unit's representative, and that these three change orders are invalid. Guoli Company insists that all six change orders are valid. Upon review, although two of the six change orders do not bear the signature of the construction unit's representative, they were all proposed by Zhenye Company, signed by representatives of Zhenye Company, Guoli Company, and the supervising unit, and then sealed by both parties. Since the contract in question was performed between the two parties, Zhenye Company, as the employer, had the obligation to submit the change orders to the construction unit and design unit for signature. Even if there was a defect in failing to obtain the relevant representative's signature, this cannot be a reason for Zhenye Company to deny the validity of the change orders. Therefore, the first-instance court did not err in confirming the validity of the six change orders. The appeal by Zhenye Company that some change orders should be deemed invalid due to lack of signatures from the construction unit, etc., is not sustained.

Although Zhenye Company claims to have paid the full project payment, it cannot provide effective evidence to prove this. Therefore, the first-instance court had no choice but to use the evidence provided by Guoli Company as the basis for calculating the project payment. Although Zhenye Company requested that the amount of the project payment be determined through appraisal, this request was not supported because it failed to pay the appraisal fee on time. However, Zhenye Company still retains the right to defense on the issue of determining the project payment amount. This Court should still review its defense. Zhenye Company argues that due to an error in Guoli Company's calculation, the project payment amount determined in the first-instance judgment was overcalculated by RMB 1,879,343.98. During the second instance of this Court, Guoli Company confirmed the miscalculation and expressly stated that it waives its claim against Zhenye Company for RMB 1,879,343.98 in project payment. This Court confirms this waiver in accordance with the law. Zhenye Company's defense that the first-instance judgment overcalculated the above project payment is justified, and this Court sustains it.

(3) Whether the First-Instance Judgment Correctly Applied Article 20 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts. The prerequisite for applying this article of the judicial interpretation is that the parties have agreed that if the employer fails to respond within the agreed period after receiving the completion settlement documents, it shall be deemed to have approved the completion settlement documents. In this case, the parties only chose to use the standard form contract for construction project construction contracts formulated by the Ministry of Construction, but did not make a special agreement on whether the completion settlement documents submitted by the contractor would be used as the basis for the project payment in such circumstances. Therefore, it cannot be simply inferred from the provisions of Article 33, Paragraph 3 of the general terms of this standard form contract that the employer has recognized the completion settlement documents submitted by the contractor as the basis for determining the project payment amount. Zhenye Company's appeal that Article 20 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation should not be applied in this case is well-founded, and this Court sustains it.

The non-application of Article 20 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation in this case does not mean that the provisions of Article 33, Paragraph 3 of the general terms of the Construction Project Construction Contract are not binding on the parties. Violating this provision still incurs liability for breach of contract. The reason for upholding the first-instance judgment's conclusion of using the completion settlement documents submitted by Guoli Company to Zhenye Company as the basis for confirming the project payment amount is that, during the first-instance proceedings, after Guoli Company submitted the completion settlement documents as evidence for determining the project payment amount, Zhenye Company failed to provide contrary evidence within the evidence submission period designated by the first-instance court, nor did it apply for appraisal within that period. After the first-instance court agreed to conduct an appraisal on matters related to the project payment, Zhenye Company, on the grounds that it disagreed with the scope of appraisal determined by the first-instance court, failed to pay the appraisal fee within the period designated by the department responsible for commissioning appraisal work in the first-instance court, resulting in the appraisal not being carried out. Zhenye Company should bear the consequences of failing to provide evidence. Under these circumstances, the people's court can only use the evidence provided by one party as the basis for confirming the project payment.

(4) Whether the First-Instance Procedure Was Illegal. Based on the application for property preservation filed by Guoli Company and the guarantee provided by Jiangxi Lianyou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., the first-instance court lawfully ordered the freezing, seizure, and attachment of Zhenye Company's property. Subsequently, based on the Application for Advance Execution submitted by Guoli Company and a separate guarantee provided by Jiangxi Lianyou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., the court lawfully ordered the payment of RMB 2,000,000 from the frozen funds to Guoli Company to be used to pay the wages of migrant workers owed by Guoli Company, among other things. Zhenye Company's claim that Guoli Company did not provide a guarantee is inconsistent with the facts. The advance execution measures taken by the first-instance court met the statutory conditions. The failure to conduct the appraisal of the project cost in the first instance was due to Zhenye Company's abandonment of its right to appraisal. Guoli Company did not list the construction unit of the project, Jinxian County People's Government, or the developer, Zhenchang Company, as third parties. Neither of the latter two applied to participate in the litigation, and neither is a bearer of obligations under the contract in question. Therefore, the first-instance court did not err in not adding them as third parties. Zhenye Company's appeal that the first-instance procedure was illegal is unfounded, and this Court does not accept it.

(5) Calculation of Interest on the Project Payment. Zhenye Company's appeal request to dismiss all of Guoli Company's claims should include the dismissal of Guoli Company's claim for interest on the project payment. During the second instance of this Court, Guoli Company, by way of a Confirmation Letter, expressed its waiver of interest of RMB 600,000 on the project payment. Guoli Company's above expression of intent is genuine and does not violate legal provisions, and this Court confirms it. According to the contract signed by the parties, interest on the project payment should accrue from the 29th day after Guoli Company submitted the completion settlement report to Zhenye Company. Since the total interest claimed by Guoli Company at the time of filing the lawsuit was RMB 900,000, deducting the voluntarily waived amount of RMB 600,000, the interest on the project payment claimed by Guoli Company shall be limited to RMB 300,000. Because the interest calculated at the same-period benchmark lending rate of the People's Bank of China totals more than RMB 300,000, the interest on the project payment to be received by Guoli Company shall be RMB 300,000.

In conclusion, the first-instance judgment contained errors in calculating the project payment amount and determining the starting date for interest, and improperly applied the law. It should be corrected in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2005) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 5 of the Jiangxi High People's Court is modified as follows: Jiangxi Zhenye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall pay Jiangxi Guoli Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. RMB 6,394,467.67 in project payment and interest of RMB 300,000 within 15 days from the date this judgment takes effect.

If the monetary obligation determined in this judgment is not performed within the time limit, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances total RMB 150,020, and the property preservation fee is RMB 65,520, totaling RMB 215,540. Jiangxi Zhenye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear 65%, i.e., RMB 140,101; Jiangxi Guoli Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. shall bear 35%, i.e., RMB 75,439.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Han Mei

Judge: Zhang Jinxian

Judge: Wu Xiaofang

March 13, 2007

Clerk: Wei Da

[Brief Introduction of the Presiding Judge]

Han Mei, Senior Judge: Born in 1962, Master of Laws, served as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2000.
